reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about debinding mechanisms, carbon retention effects, and resulting property improvements, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific behavior of this AlCrFeNiSi powder/resin system under the proposed debinding atmospheres.
premises: Oxygen-rich debinding causes rapid oxidation, excessive CO/CO2 evolution, pressure-driven cracks, and surface oxide layers that inhibit densification
Oxygen-deficient debinding results in incomplete carbon oxidation, diminished gas evolution, and limited pore formation
Retained carbon under oxygen-deficient conditions reduces pore volume and surface cracking
Retained carbon promotes interparticle diffusion and bonding, enabling earlier consolidation at ~50°C lower sintering temperature
Oxygen-deficient debinding yields comparable compressive strength (~5.1 MPa) with reduced residual thermal stresses
